post_text:
Waldorf Astoria opened its first hotel in Malaysia on 30 October: 268 suites in Kuala Lumpur's Golden Triangle, and not one standard room.

The smallest suite measures 80 m². The Waldorf Astoria Suite reaches 745 m². Interiors are by Deboss Collective, and the art was curated with the Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia.

General manager @Etienne Dalançon, formerly at the helm of Waldorf Astoria Maldives Ithaafushi, leads the opening. Within Hilton, the region is run by @Alan Watts, President, Asia Pacific.

Dining is a draw in its own right. Three of the seven restaurants and bars are concepts by Jean-Georges Vongerichten of @Jean-Georges Management, and Yaari was created with Garima Arora, the chef of Gaa in Bangkok. The spa covers 2,275 m² over two floors.

La Revue des Hôtels found mid-November rates from RM 3,489, about €770, taxes included.

The signal: Kuala Lumpur has long been one of Asia's most affordable luxury capitals. An all-suite hotel lets @Waldorf Astoria Hotels & Resorts sell space rather than a room category, and test a new price ceiling for the city.

Would you pay a premium for a suite-only hotel in a city known for value?
